requirement:
HC represents a FIXME acknowledgment as a graph node and exposes its tracking
issue relationships as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes. A named FIXME also
connects the acknowledgment to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges;
an unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
Each issue named by the acknowledgment is available through its tracking edges.
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph` has these testable obligations:
- A FIXME acknowledgment is a graph node.
- Its tracking-issue relationships are labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes.
- A named FIXME also connects to the requirement it acknowledges.
- An unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
- Every issue the acknowledgment names is reachable through those tracking edges.

The `references` tool lists no `{test}`, `{impl}` or `{cite}` sites for this requirement. A search of `src/sdk.rs` found no test touching FIXME nodes or tracking edges.

`HabeasNode` in `src/sdk.rs` has no FIXME or GitHub-issue variants, and `outgoing_edges` in `src/sdk.rs` only maps an `Acknowledges` label to "fixme". So none of the obligations has a test: named vs. unnamed connections, source ownership, and multiple issue targets are all untested.

This gap is acknowledged. `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` carries a `{fixme}` for `requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph`. Its body says the FIXME graph nodes and tracking-issue edges are deferred and that named/unnamed acknowledgments, source ownership and multiple issue targets have no tests. That is the same gap I found. The issue it names, nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26, is open, and I found nothing showing that tests now exist. The acknowledgment is therefore still accurate and in force.
